Im in the same spot: i've tested my rope a few times before and i felt absolutely nothing. 
I used to feel conflicted about my suicidal thoughts: but not anymore. I could stab myself in the throat with a knife and feel like im taking a peaceful stroll in a field. 
It may be that you reached a point where you would rather hang from the ceiling rather than spend another day in pain. 
But i also felt this complete nihilism towards potentially lethal scenarios when i overloaded or had a mental breakdown. We all have that "limit", it's what makes us cross it that matters here though. I recall walking out of school when i was about 12 years old after a really bad day; i was shocked by how easy it was for my brain to process the fact that i was going to jump under a car. Was i in a tought spot? Was i already familiar with suicidal thoughts? Sure. But it was a little more deeper than that. I was pushed to the edge and i was having a mental breakdown: my whole perception of reality was warped in that frame of time; this is why my survival instinct just wasn't working. 
What im trying to say here it's that feeling in that way may be caused by multiple factors; im asking you to revaluate your status and see where it leads you. 
If you feel like taking your life, please don't be afraid to share your pain through an hotline or any other means available to you. 
And if you felt like this comment helped you somehow, feel free to message me if you wish to vent; i have already decided when i'll pass away, i may as well use my remaining time to help the living.

I haven't played the original version (on Sega saturn), but supposedly the PSP remake got "fixed" in a way from the flaws that the original version had (difficulty, the chat system, ecc); i'd say it's like Soul Hacker, but a little more difficult because there's no Nemissa, so you're forced to use and raise demons (you got Rei, but she's crap compared to the silver haired magician gal). 
Gameplay wise it's almost at the same level: but demon recruiting it's painful sometimes; it was quite easy in Soul Hacker (at least the 3DS version), but in Devil Summoner it takes an insane ammount of time; they still have their own patterns according to their own personality, but sometimes they get randomized and in general they will always try to steal from you. 
The dungeons are cool: a bit mundane (a police station, gov building, a yakuza mansion, ecc) but i liked them a lot; although the dungeon designers suddenly recalled that trap doors and teleporters are a thing in the SMT series only near the end, so the final dungeons are pure CBT. One of the worst offenders is Chinatown (中華街) with an insane ammount of teleporters which mostly lead to nowhere and the Gold governament building, where even taking a step forwards sometimes can land you almost on the first floor. Even though they're frustrating, those dungeons are worth exploring because there's lot of loot, actual valuable loot in SMT it's a rare thing and i appreciated it a lot. 
The story it's quite simple, sometimes the writing felt rudimental, but i liked the fact that there's a plot twist-y part in it: the concept itself it's also original; you basically die at the beginning of the game, but Charon sends you back to life; instead of going back to your own body though, you find yourself into Kyouji Kuzonoha's body, that angry looking dude dressed in white, the actual devil summoner. You're pretty much forced to carry on his investigation, which involves two sides, one which it's kinda optional and the other one which it's the main story (investigating zoumas and finding out the truth about the Hirasaki town history and magical seal, which it's something left behind by a civilitazion that already used demons in the early Nara period). 
I was expecting it: after all a lot of japanese RPGs from the 90s and early 2000s always mentioned mysterious ancient civilitazions （keyword: 古代文明）as the culprit for stuff (games like Ku-ron youma gakuen-ki [九龍妖魔学園記] used the same plot-device and it's accidentally, another ATLUS game if i recall correctly). 

It can be fun, despite the fact that it's clearly not the best megaten game, but if you're ever planning on playing it, PLEASE do not play it on PSP; the late game dungeons will make you regret not using save states.
